title: Instrumental variables by two-stage least squares (Mendelian randomization)
summary: The effect of an exposure confounded by something unmeasured, using a genetic instrument, with the first-stage F and a robust standard error.

sizing._why: IV power depends on the instrument's strength (the first-stage R squared) as well as the effect; the catalog forms ignore it and would over-promise by a large factor. Simulation, or an MR power calculator.

pinned_defaults: R: ivreg(y ~ ldl | allele_score); HC1 sandwich; the first-stage F from summary(diagnostics = TRUE).

Python: 2SLS written out (no new dependency), with the structural residuals y - X b computed from the OBSERVED exposure. Running the stages as two OLS fits reproduces the coefficient and gives an SE 28% too large here.
Both: HC1 robust SE, conventional SE beside it.
_assumptions: Relevance (checkable: F about 300 here), independence from confounders, and exclusion (no path from the instrument to the outcome except through the exposure). The last two are arguments, not tests.
